questions.text: To study opinions of 440 students, which plan best avoids selection bias?
answers: Let only enthusiastic volunteers respond
Survey only a favorite club
Survey only students buying one lunch item
Randomly select students from the full school list
questions.explanation: A random sample from the full target population gives different students a chance to be included.

questions.text: A school has 640 students. A survey samples 29 students. What is the size of the population?

questions.text: A school wants to estimate all students’ favorite lunch. It surveys only students in the pizza line. Which improvement best reduces bias?
answers: Ask only students who volunteer online
Ask more students in the pizza line
Randomly sample students across the whole school
Remove answers that disagree with the principal
questions.explanation: The sampling frame should include the population, not only one preference group.

questions.text: A random sample of 60 students from one middle school is surveyed about travel to school. Which population is the sample intended to represent?

Students at that middle school
Only the 60 students, because samples can never estimate a population
Every student in the state
